thesis_summary.thesis: CrowdStrike Holdings sells cloud-native endpoint and identity security software on a subscription model. Customers pay recurring fees for the Falcon platform, which consolidates threat detection, response, and adjacent modules (identity, cloud workload, log management). Revenue reached $4.81 billion in fiscal 2026 (year ended January 31, 2026) per `CRWD/investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260305_rpt20260131_acc0001535527_26_000010.htm`. The company generates substantial cash from operations ($1.61 billion in fiscal 2026) while reporting a GAAP net loss ($162.5 million) because stock-based compensation and acquisition-related costs remain large relative to reported earnings.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market prices CrowdStrike as a premium-growth compounder after the July 2024 Falcon content-update incident, yet filing cash economics already support more than $1.3 billion of normalized owner earnings. Investors may overweight GAAP losses and headline churn fears while underweighting operating cash flow that grew 29% compounded over five years and net cash of roughly $4.0 billion against modest long-term debt. If module adoption and net retention stabilize post-incident, owner cash can grow faster than the screening-grade reinvestment template assumes; conversely, if incident-related churn or elevated sales and marketing persist, owner cash could compress toward the low-case bridge typed in the prospective falsifier.
